claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let me start by asking: **Do you have any children that you're responsible for?** If yes, how many children do you have, and what are their ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex who's 11 years old. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can help you determine if you're eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me ask you a few questions to assess your eligibility:

**Does Alex normally live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me - he lives with his mum.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's an important factor in determining eligibility.

**Do you contribute towards Alex's upbringing costs?** For example, do you pay maintenance or child support for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do help out. I contribute towards his upkeep - I give money for things like his clothes, school stuff, and other things he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying that. Let me read the relevant guidance to better understand the rules when a child lives with someone else.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for waiting. I've reviewed the relevant guidance. I have a few more questions to help determine your eligibility:

**Is Alex's mum currently claiming Child Benefit for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she's not claiming it currently.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a couple more questions:

**Are the contributions you make towards Alex's upkeep at least equal to or more than the Child Benefit payment amount?** (Child Benefit is currently £25.60 per week for the eldest or only child, which works out to about £110-111 per month.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I contribute £50 a week towards his upkeep, so that's definitely more than the Child Benefit amount.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. One final question:

**Is Alex under 16 years old, or if he's 16 or over, is he in approved education or training?** (I believe you mentioned he's 11, but I just want to confirm he meets the age requirements.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex is 11, so he's definitely under 16.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

Even though Alex doesn't live with you, you can still claim Child Benefit because:

1. **Alex is under 16** - He's 11 years old, so he meets the age requirement
2. **You contribute sufficiently to his upkeep** - You're paying £50 per week towards Alex's costs (clothes, school supplies, etc.), which is more than the Child Benefit amount of £25.60 per week
3. **You live in the UK** - You meet the residency requirement
4. **No one else is claiming** - Alex's mum is not currently claiming Child Benefit for him

According to UK Child Benefit rules, you're considered "responsible for" a child if you're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards looking after them, even if they don't live with you.

**Important points to note:**
- Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at any time
- You should be aware of the High Income Child Benefit tax charge if you or a partner earn over £60,000 per year
- You'll need to make a claim for Child Benefit if you want to receive it

Would you like any additional information about making a claim?
